MANILA, Philippines — Ten new National Artists have been named by Malacañang, according to an official Palace communiqué yesterday.
The latest batch is the first group of National Artists named since 2022 and brings the total number of recipients of the country's highest recognition for Filipino artists to 91.

The list includes: Gabby Formoso (Architecture) Nonoy Froilan (Dance) Patis Tesoro (Fashion) Armando 'Bing' Lao (Film and Broadcast Arts) Gregorio Brillantes (Literature) Nicanor Tiongson (Literature) Fred Buenaventura (Music) Teddy Hilado (Theater) Imelda Cajipe Endaya (Visual Arts) Nunelucio Alvarado (Visual Arts) Proclamation 1414, dated September 1, was signed by the President to proclaim the ten Filipinos as National Artists.

The new National Artists are architect Gabriel Formoso (+), dancer Rafael “Nonoy” Froilan, designer Maria Beatriz “Patis” Tesoro, scriptwriter Armando Lao (+), writer Gregorio Brillantes (+), playwright-scholar Nicanor Tiongson, composer Alfredo Buenaventura, lighting designer Teodoro Hilado (+), artist Imelda Cajipe Endaya and painter Nunelucio Alvarado of Negros Occidental.

Proclamation No. 1414 declared the latest batch of National Artists for 2025 in a letter addressed to Kaye Tinga, president and CEO of the Cultural Center of the Philippines, from the Office of the President.

The 76-year-old is the first woman to be named national artist in the visual arts category.
Born on October 24, 1950, in Calbiga, Samar, Rafael “Nonoy” Froilan is one of the Philippines’ most celebrated male ballet dancers and has come to be known as the country’s premier danseur.
Froilan trained with the University of the East Dance Troupe before joining the CCP Dance School in 1972 and Ballet Philippines the following year.

For more than two decades, he served as principal dancer of Ballet Philippines, originating roles created specifically for him, including Norman Walker’s Songs of a Wayfarer and National Artist Alice Reyes’ Rama Hari and Carmina Burana .
He also famously danced opposite Dame Margot Fonteyn and Yoko Morishita.
He has spent decades teaching at the Philippine High School for the Arts.
In 2020, he received the Gawad CCP Para sa Sining for Dance.
– with reports from Arabella Grace Sta Ana and Jade Tan/Rappler.com Arabella Grace Sta Ana is a Rappler intern studying BA Philosophy at UP Los Baños.
Jade Tan is a Rappler intern studying AB Journalism at UST Manila.
